data.narrative:
Telesat Lightspeed, a Space & Aerospace company at public stage led by CEO Dan Goldberg, has raised C$2.1B to date. Valuation analysis draws from a peer universe of five public-stage comparables in the same sector: SpaceX ($1.6T), Rocket Lab ($40.0B), Planet Labs ($7.6B), Firefly Aerospace ($2.9B), and Astroscale ($840M).

The peer-median method is the primary applicable triangulation approach, given that Telesat Lightspeed's revenue is not publicly disclosed. The median valuation across the five same-sector, same-stage peers is $7.6B, with a range spanning $840M at the low end (Astroscale) to $1.6T at the high end (SpaceX). This wide dispersion reflects material differences in technology maturity, market position, and funding stage within the Space & Aerospace sector. Public-comp anchoring via price-to-sales multiples (sector median: 24.6x across six tickers) cannot be applied without the target's revenue figure.

The triangulation analysis supports a valuation range of $6.4B to $8.7B, centered on $7.6B. This range is grounded in a single method, which constrains confidence. Key uncertainties include the absence of revenue visibility, the extreme heterogeneity of the peer set (particularly SpaceX as an outlier), and stage-specific factors that may differentiate Telesat Lightspeed from public comparables. Additional revenue or contract pipeline data would materially improve precision.
